questions: You present one device over two cooldowns ("The device was measured during two separate cool downs.", p. 9), and the author contributions mention "the devices" (p. 8). How many devices did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed fractional Coulomb blockade and the even-odd pattern?
Why were the other devices set aside?
Which ranges of VT, VBG, Vqpc, Vedge and magnetic field did you measure beyond Table I and Extended Data Figs. 9 to 11, and in how much of that space does the merged 2e/3 regime of Fig. 4g appear?
What does the second-best example of the merging in Fig. 4f look like, for example at another |Nqp| range, in the other cooldown, or for 2/3 quasiholes?

Table I lists Fig. 1h as "νbulk = 2/5, νdot = 1/3" (p. 10), while the text says "For νedge ≈ νbulk = ν = 1/3, Vdot has no measurable effect on the conductance" (p. 3). Which bulk filling applies to Fig. 1h–j and Fig. 4a, and does it change the e/3 reading of the spacing?
Did you check leakage on all seven gates at the Fig. 4 settings, and did you repeat the Fig. 4e–g sweeps to show the merging recurs at the same VT?

The e/3 assignment from the spacing ratio rests on "Assuming these phenomenological parameters are determined primarily by geometry, and therefore ignoring any dependence on Nqp or ν" (p. 3). Did you measure the magnetic-field period of the resonances at fixed gates, which would give the tunneling charge without that assumption?

Could a transition with weak edge-to-dot coupling go unseen in the merged regime? You note the coupling can be "too small to resolve the backscattering current" (p. 5) and that the dip finding "may miss resonances as they emerge" (Extended Data Fig. 10, p. 23). Does the weak sector's width in Fig. 4f shrink to zero while both lines stay visible?
